editorial.headline: Soybean Farming With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01113 covers the integrated cultivation of soybeans, with foreign ownership open nationally and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01113 is a clean agricultural classification for soybean farming. Its core activity is the practical chain of growing soybeans: preparing the land, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and carrying out post-harvest work when those steps form one connected farming operation. The record also brings soybean seed activity into the same frame when it is part of the soybean crop cycle. In plain terms, this is not a trading, processing, or advisory category; it is the agricultural work of producing soybeans from land to harvest, including the crop-handling steps that belong to that same farming sequence.

That integrated character matters because it defines who this code is for. A founder registering under it is not merely touching soybeans at one isolated point. The activity described is cultivation-led: land preparation, planting, crop care, harvest, and post-harvest as a single operational chain. The record opens this classification across every business scale listed: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means it is not reserved only for a large plantation-style setup, nor confined to the smallest agricultural operator. It can describe a small farming enterprise, a medium agricultural business, or a larger soybean cultivation operation, provided the registered activity remains within the scope stated in the record.

Nationally, the position on foreign investment is clear. Its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. So, on the national record supplied here, this is a classification a foreign-owned company may use without a foreign shareholding cap below full ownership. That is the decisive national point: the activity is open for PMA, and the ceiling given in the record reaches 100%. There is no basis in the slim record to add extra capital thresholds, licensing steps, special permits, tax treatments, or timing assumptions, so the clean reading is simply that the national PMA door is open for this soybean farming activity.

The Bali picture is also unusually clear. The record says this code is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but the Bali reason states that the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a hidden warning dressed up as access: a foreign investor can read this record as nationally open and not Bali-blocked, while still staying within the exact agricultural scope of soybean cultivation and seed activity described here.
